sentences.text: Prosecution Case:
The marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Kannika B. K. and the accused No.1 was solemnized on 03-09-2017 as per Hindu customs and rites.
At that time, the accused demanded and received 200 grams of gold ornaments, Rs.3 lakhs in cash and Rs.50,000/- for clothes as dowry from CW4 namely Sri Kullegowda and CW5 namely Smt Vedavathi.

After the marriage, CW1 was residing at house No.7, 1st Cross, Srikrupa Layout, Abbigere within the limits of Gangammanagudi Police Station, Bengaluru with accused persons wherein the accused No.1 to 4 with common intention subjected the CW1 to mental and physical cruelty for fetching additional dowry amount and accused No.3 insisted CW1 to give her salary to accused No.4.

Further the accused No.2 provoked the accused No.1 for ousting CW1 from house and incited him to marry another girl who could give him a house in Bengaluru and by which subjected the CW1 to mental and physical cruelty.
Further the accused No.1 to 4 were forced CW1 to fetch a house in Bengaluru from her father CW4 and Rs.20 lakhs as additional dowry amount to do business.
Thereby accused persons committed the alleged offences.
3. First Information Report:

On the basis of first information given by informant cum CW1, the Sri H.V.Venkatachalaiah, CW11/PI of Gangammanagudi Police Station registered Crime KABC030515302019 CC No.16298/2019 No.14/2019 against the accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable under Section 498(A) read with Sec.34 IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D.P. Act, prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court.

4. Investigation: Thereafter, he drawn spot mahazar as per Ex.P2 on 04-02-2019, recorded the statements of requisite witnesses, collected the documents and submitted the charge sheet against accused No.1 t 4 for the alleged offences.
5.
On receipt of charge sheet, this Court took cognizance of offences alleged against the accused persons.
6. The accused No.1 to 4 were enlarged on bail by the order dated 16-11-2019.
7. Copies of prosecution papers as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused persons.
8. Charge:

After hearing learned Sr.APP and counsel for accused persons, charge for the offences punishable U/Sec.498(A) read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, has been framed, read over and explained to the accused persons in the language KABC030515302019 CC No.16298/2019 known to them, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
9. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 11 witnesses and examined 1 witness and exhibited 5 documents.

The learned Senior APP prayed for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that no purpose would be served as PW1 and the accused have compromised the matrimonial differences in M.C.

sentences.text: Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: There are no incriminating evidences against the accused found from the evidence of prosecution thereby the recording of statement of accused as per Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with.
11. Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

12. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
KABC030515302019 CC No.16298/2019 1.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that at the time of marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Kannika with accused No.1 on 03-09-2017, the accused No.1 to 4 were demanded and received 200 grams of gold ornaments, Rs.3 lakhs in cash and Rs.50,000/- for clothes as dowry from CW4 namely Sri Kullegowda and CW5 namely Smt Vedavathi., thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Sec.3 of Dowry Prohibition Act?
2.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after marriage, CW1 started residing at house No.7, 1st Cross, Srikrupa Layout, Abbigere within the limits of Gangammanagudi Police Station, Bengaluru with accused wherein the accused No.1 to 4 with common intention subjected the CW1 to mental and physical cruelty for KABC030515302019 CC No.16298/2019 fetching additional dowry amount and property thereby resulted in commission of the offences punishable under Sec.498(A) read with Section 34 of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said duration, the accused persons harassed CW1 for fetching additional dowry amount of Rs.20 lakhs and property from her parental house thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Sec.4 of Dowry Prohibition Act?
4. What order?

13. The findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 to 3 : In the Negative Point No.4 : As per final order KABC030515302019 CC No.16298/2019 REASONS 14.
Point No.1 to 3: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution has examined one witness, which is as follows:

4 i. CW1 by name Smt. Kannika B K , being informant examined as PW1 and identified her signatures on Ex.P1 (Complaint) and Ex.P2(Spot Mahazar) as Ex.P1(a) and 2(a)
and deposed that when she went to the police station for sorting out the minor differences of opinion amongst her and the accused No. 1, the police obtained her signatures on the said documents and she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 and further stated that she did not lodge complaint against accused and no mahazar was conducted in her presence.

On perusal of aforesaid recitation, it is clear that the disputes between the accused No.1 and CW1 (informant) have been settled.

16. This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana and anr in the case of AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that, KABC030515302019 CC No.16298/2019 "in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.

entities.text: B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: and in the case of Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat), wherein this lordship observed which runs thus:

entities.text: Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

Although, Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code is not compoundable, but in the nature and circumstances of the case and the situation prevailing, accord is hereby granted to compromise the dispute between the parties and hence joint petition filed in both the cases are hereby allowed."

It further held that after examining the nature of the case and the circumstances,
KABC030515302019 CC No.16298/2019 under which the offence has been committed, it would be proper to compound the offence and in my opinion, it would be also meet the ends of justice."
ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the PW1 and accused No.1 have been resolved.
The criminal case under Section 498(A) of IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D.P. Act is the off-shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.
The parties have come to their terms and in pursuance thereto the CW1/PW1 does not intend to proceed with this case and hence she has not supported the prosecution case.

17. In the case of the KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464,
wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".

entities.text: KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18. Under these circumstances and on account of the preposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex and Hon'ble High Court, even if other witnesses examined KABC030515302019 CC No.16298/2019 by the prosecution, they did supported the prosecution, would not helpful to the prosecution.
Under these circumstances, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned Sr.APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the ingredients for offences Under Section 498(A) of IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D.P. Act was not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answer the point No.1 to 3 in the Negative.
19. Point No.4:-

In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1 to 3, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused No.1 to 4 are found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Sec.498(A) read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
KABC030515302019 CC No.16298/2019 (ii) Accused are set at liberty.
(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C their bail bonds shall be in force for 6 (six) months.
(iv) Ordered accordingly.
